items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the county law, in relation to a 9-8-8 suicide prevention and
mental health crisis hotline system
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6194

SPONSOR: BROUK
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the county law, in relation to a 9-8-8
suicide prevention and mental health crisis hotline system


 
PURPOSE:

To establish a three-digit, 9-8-8 suicide prevention and mental health
crisis hotline system that will save lives by connecting people experi-
encing mental health crisis with compassionate, lifesaving, and
culturally competent mental health care services.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1. The short title of this bill is "9-8-8 Suicide Prevention and
Mental Health Crisis Act"

Section 2. Adds a new Article 6-B to the county law. The new article
contains five sections as follows:

§ 340 sets forth definitions.

§ 341 Requires the commissioner of the department of public service, the
commissioner of the office of mental health and the commissioner of
addiction services and supports to designate on or before July 16, 2022,
a crisis hotline center or centers to provide crisis care coordination
to individuals accessing the 9-8-8 suicide prevention and mental health
crisis hotline from anywhere within New York State 24 hours a day, 7
days a week; requires the the commissioner of the office of mental
health and the commissioner of addiction services and supports to submit
an annual report on the 9-8-8 suicide prevention and mental health
crisis hotline's usage, services and impact.

§ 342 Requires the commissioner of the office of mental health and the
commissioner of addiction services and supports to provide onsite
response services using mobile crisis teams; defines the types of
personnel that will comprise mobile crisis teams.

§ 343 Requires the commissioner of the department of taxation and
finance, the commissioner of the office of mental health and the commis-
sioner of addiction services and supports to establish and maintain a
9-8-8 trust fund; prohibits monies in the 9-8-8 trust fund from being
transferred or used for other purposes; and requires the commissioner of
the department of taxation and finance, the commissioner of the office
of mental health and the commissioner of addiction services and supports
to submit an annual report of all fund deposits and expenditures into
the 9-8-8 trust fund to the Governor, Temporary President of the Senate,
Speaker of the Assembly, Minority Leader of the Senate, Minority Leader
of the Assembly, and the Chair of the Federal Communications Commission.

§ 344 Requires the commissioner of the department of public service to
establish a monthly fee at a fixed rate on each New York resident that
subscribes to cell phone and text message services. This monthly fee
shall be used for the operation and maintenance of a 9-8-8-suicide
prevention and mental health crisis system and the continuum of services
provided. Individuals who are subscribers to the federal lifeline
program are exempt from this monthly fee.
Section 3. This act shall take effect immediately.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

According to the American Foundation for Suicide Prevention, suicide is
the 12th leading cause of death in New York. In 2020, for every 100,000
New Yorkers, 8.28 lose their life to suicide. Suicide is the second
leading death for people between the ages of 10 and 34 years old. For
individuals between the ages of 35 and 54, suicide is the fourth leading
cause of death.

On October 19, 2020, the National Suicide Prevention Designation Act was
signed into law to transform the ten-digit, 800-273-8255 number into an
easy to remember, three-digit, 9-8-8 number that will connect individ-
uals at risk for suicide, as well as those experiencing mental health
and substance abuse crises, to trained, National Suicide Prevention
Lifeline counselors. Currently, 9-1-1 is the only system used for all
emergencies, including mental health emergencies. This new 9-8-8 life-
line puts in practice a safer and more equitable response to mental
health, substance abuse, and suicidal crises.  Mental health crisis
calls can result in potentially dangerous and traumatizing outcomes when
police are called, particularly in underserved and underrepresented
communities. This appeared vividly evident in Rochester, NY, on the
evening of March 23, 2020, when Daniel Prude, a 41-year-old African
American man, was injured after being physically restrained by City of
Rochester police officers.  Daniel Prude was suffering from a mental
health episode after ingesting PCP and was walking naked in the city's
streets. The officers placed a spit hood over Mr. Prude's head after he
began spitting while he sat naked on the ground during winter weather. A
week later, Mr. Prude succumbed to his injuries and died.

Unfortunately, this situation in Rochester, NY, is not unique and is one
of the countless examples across the state and country of the conse-
quences of not providing the most appropriate response to a mental
health or substance abuse crisis. This legislation would promote public
health, safety, and welfare to people experiencing mental health or
substance crises. It would better ensure that these individuals experi-
encing mental health or substance abuse crisis receive appropriate and
compassionate care from trained culturally competent responders.  Ameri-
can Foundation for Suicide Prevention. (2021, February 9).  Suicide
Facts and Figures: New York. Retrieved March 31, 2021, from
https://aws-fetch.s3.amazonaws.com/state-fact-
sheets/2021/2021-state-fact-sheets-new-york.pdf

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

TBD.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

An act to amend the county law, the tax law and the state finance law,
in relation to a 9-8-8 suicide prevention and mental health crisis

Section 3. Amends Section 186-f of the Tax Law.

Section 4. Provides for up to eighty million dollars to be deposited

mental health crisis hotline fund. This section also requires the comp-

annual report of fund deposits and expenditures made into the suicide

nications commission.

tation with the commissioners of the office of mental health and the
office of addiction services and supports to establish the 988 surcharge
on New York residents that subscribe to telecommunications services.
Individuals who are subscribers to the federal lifeline program are
exempt from this monthly surcharge.

Section 7. Sets forth an immediate effective date.

cause of death.

signed into law to transform the ten-digit, 800-273-8255 number into an
easy to remember, three-digit, 9-8-8 number that will connect individ-
uals at risk for suicide, as well as those experiencing mental health
and substance abuse crises, to trained, National Suicide Prevention
Lifeline counselors. Currently, 9-1-1 is the only system used for all
emergencies, including mental health emergencies. This new 9-8-8 life-
line puts in practice a safer and more equitable response to mental
health, substance abuse, and suicidal crises.

New Bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

TBD.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

BILL NUMBER: S6194B

SPONSOR: BROUK
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the county law, in relation to a 9-8-8 suicide
prevention and mental health crisis hotline system

 
PURPOSE:

To establish a three-digit, 9-8-8 suicide prevention and mental health
crisis hotline system that will save lives by connecting people experi-
encing mental health crisis with compassionate, lifesaving, and
culturally competent mental health care services.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

A7177-B would do the following:

*Provide definitions

*Require the commissioner of the department of public service, the
commissioner of the office of mental health and the commissioner of
addiction services and supports to designate on or before July 16, 2022,
a crisis hotline center

*Establish minimum standards a crisis hotline is required to meet;

*Authorizes the department of public service, the office of mental
health, and the office of addiction supports and services to have joint
oversight of suicide prevention and crisis service activities and coor-
dination of crisis centers to ensure consistency of public messages for
988 services;

*Establish training guidelines for 988 crisis hotline staff, 911 opera-
tors, and first responders

*Require the commissioner of the office of mental health and the commis-
sioner of addiction services and supports to submit an annual report on
the 9-8-8 suicide prevention and mental health crisis hotline's usage,
services and impact.

*Require the commissioner of the office of mental health, in consulta-
tion with the commissioners of the office of addiction services and
supports, the department of taxation and finance, and the department of
public service to submit a report that details the resources necessary
to make the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline, available, opera-
tional, and effective across the state, including an evaluation of
available and new revenue sources to support the implementation, staff-
ing, and ongoing activities of 9-8- 8 services that are reasonably
attributed to:(a) ensuring the efficient and effective routing of calls
made to the NSPL to an appropriate 9-8-8 crisis hotline center; (b)
personnel and the provision of mental health, crisis outreach and
stabilization services directly related to the NSPL; and (c) the estab-
lishment of a trust fund for the purpose of depositing any dedicated
revenues collected to create and maintain a statewide 9-8-8 suicide
prevention and mental health crisis hotline system. The report shall be
submitted on or before December thirty-first, two thousand twenty-one to

the governor, the speaker of the assembly, the temporary president of
the senate, and the minority leaders of the senate and the assembly.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

According to the American Foundation for Suicide Prevention, suicide is
the 12th leading cause of death in New York. In 2020, for every 100,000
New Yorkers, 8.28 lose their life to suicide. Suicide is the second
leading death for people between the ages of 10 and 34 years old. For
individuals between the ages of 35 and 54, suicide is the fourth leading
cause of death.

signed into law to transform the ten-digit, 800-273-8255 number into an
easy to remember, three-digit, 9-8-8 number that will connect individ-
uals at risk for suicide, as well as those experiencing mental health
and substance abuse crises, to trained, National Suicide Prevention
Lifeline counselors. Currently, 9-1-1 is the only system used for all
emergencies, including mental health emergencies. This new 9-8-8 life-
line puts in practice a safer and more equitable response to mental
health, substance abuse, and suicidal crises.

New Bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

TBD.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 145 Chapter 793
 
       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 6194-B, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to  amend  the  county law, in relation to a 9-8-8 suicide
        prevention and mental health crisis hotline system"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This bill  amends  the  County  Law  relating  to  the  9-8-8  suicide
prevention  and  mental  health  crisis  hotline system. The legislation
provides for definitions and provisions to implement  statewide  suicide
prevention  and  crisis  intervention services for individuals accessing
the 9-8-8 hotline.  The bill requires the Department of  Public  Service
(PSC),  in  consultation  with the Office of Mental Health (OMH) and the
Office of Alcoholism and Substance Abuse Services (OASAS)  to  designate
9-8-8  crisis  call  centers.    The bill also requires OMH and OASAS to
compile a list of reporting metrics. This bill requires OMH, in  consul-
tation  with  OASAS, PSC, and the Department of Taxation and Finance, to
issue a report to the Governor and the Legislature by December 31,  2021
detailing the resources necessary to support 9-8-8.
 
  On  October  19, 2020, the National Suicide Prevention Designation Act
was signed into law to transform  the  ten-digit  number,  800-273-8255,
into  an  easy to remember three-digit number, 9-8-8, which will connect
individuals at-risk for suicide, as well as  those  experiencing  mental
health   and   substance  abuse  crises,  to  trained  National  Suicide
Prevention Lifeline counselors. Currently, 9-1-1 is the only established
system used for all emergencies, including  behavioral  health  emergen-
cies.  This  new  9-8-8  hotline will provide a safer and more equitable
response  to  mental  health,  substance  abuse,  suicidal  crises,  and
emotional distress.
 
  However, as drafted, the bill inappropriately creates a new article in
the  County Law and also improperly designates the PSC as the lead over-
sight agency. OMH, with input from a statewide coalition of multi-disci-
plinary stakeholders, is currently  preparing  to  implement  the  9-8-8
hotline.  This is a critical initiative that requires continuous compre-
hensive planning for implementation and expansion.  I  have  reached  an
agreement with the Legislature to amend this legislation to require OMH,
in  consultation with OASAS, to provide a report to the Legislature that
outlines a plan for implementation, including recommendations for strat-
egies for identifying and supporting funding streams to  meet  projected
calls and training and cultural competence standards.
 
  Based on this agreement, I am pleased to sign this bill.

  This bill is approved.                         (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                                ______

summary: Establishes a 9-8-8 suicide prevention and mental health crisis hotline system; provides crisis intervention services and crisis care coordination to individuals accessing the 9-8-8 suicide prevention and mental health crisis hotline.
